# Data Basics {#sec-basics}

```{r}
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(nycflights13)
```

## Quick Reference: Inspecting / Overview

| Use Case                                    | Function                        | Example                                                     |
|:--------------------------------------------|:--------------------------------|:------------------------------------------------------------|
| See the first n rows                        | `head()`                        | `head(mpg, n = 10)`                                         |
| See the last n rows                         | `tail()`                        | `tail(mpg, n = 3)`                                          |
| See every column, its type and first values | `glimpse()`                     | `glimpse(flights)`                                          |
| Summary stats for each column               | `summary()`                     | `mpg |> select(hwy) |> summary()`                           |
| See the structure of the data               | `str()`                         | `str(mpg)`                                                  |
| List the column names                       | `names()`                       | `names(mpg)`                                                |
| Count the rows                              | `nrow()`                        | `nrow(flights)`                                             |
| Count missing values in every column        | `across()` inside `summarize()` | see the chunk below                                         |
| Open a spreadsheet view                     | `View()`                        | `View(flights)` !! keep out of the render with `eval: false` |
| Read the help page for a dataset/function   | `?`                             | `?mpg` (in the Console)                                     |

```{r}
# Count missing values in every column
flights |>
  summarize(across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.))))
```

## Case-by-Variable Format

- Each **row** is one case (a passenger, a flight, a car)
- Each **column** is a variable measured on that case
- **Tibbles** are the tidyverse's version of a data frame

A dataset is **tidy** when it follows three rules (more in [Tidying](tidying.qmd)):

1. Each variable is a column; each column is a variable
2. Each observation is a row; each row is an observation
3. Each value is a cell; each cell is a single value

## Column Types

Column types determine which operations are possible. For example, you can take the `mean()` of a number (`int`, `dbl`), but not of text (`chr`).

| Type     | Means                                   | Example values               |
|:---------|:----------------------------------------|:-----------------------------|
| `<int>`  | integer (whole numbers)                 | `month`, `hwy`               |
| `<dbl>`  | double (decimal numbers)                | `dep_delay`, `displ`         |
| `<chr>`  | character (text)                        | `carrier`, `class`           |
| `<lgl>`  | logical (`TRUE` / `FALSE`)              | the result of `dep_delay > 0` |
| `<fct>`  | factor (categories with a fixed order)  | study strategy in [Models](models.qmd) |

- Change a type with `as.numeric()`, `as.character()`, `factor()`
- !! A number stored as text (`"10"`) looks fine but `mean()` fails on it. Check `glimpse()` first.

## The dplyr Rules

**Every dplyr verb follows the same rules:**

1. First argument is the data frame
2. Columns are named without quotes
   - !! **Exception, pivots:** when a function *creates* new columns from text, the new names go in quotes: `pivot_longer(cols = ..., names_to = "season", values_to = "count")`. Existing columns (`cols =`) are still unquoted. See [Tidying](tidying.qmd).
   - Joins also accept quoted names: `left_join(y, by = "county_id")`
3. Output is always a **new** data frame (the original is never changed unless you save over it with `<-`)

## The Pipe `|>`

The pipe means "and then".

- Passes the result on its left into the first argument of the function on its right
- Because of rule 1, every dplyr verb can be chained

```{r}
# "Take flights, AND THEN keep Seattle flights, AND THEN count them by carrier"
flights |>
  filter(dest == "SEA") |>
  count(carrier, sort = TRUE)
```

## Vectors and `c()`

A **vector** is a list of values that are all the same type. `c()` ("combine") makes one.

```{r}
seattle_area <- c("SEA", "BFI", "PAE")  # character vector
delays <- c(5, -2, 30, NA)              # numeric vector
length(seattle_area)
mean(delays, na.rm = TRUE)
```

| Where I've used `c()` | Example |
|:---------------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Several columns at once | `select(c(year, month, day))`, `pivot_longer(cols = c(q1, q2))` |
| Several values to match | `filter(dest %in% c("SEA", "PDX"))` (below) |
| New column names | `separate(ht, into = c("feet", "inches"))` |
| Join on several keys | `left_join(per_game, by = c("player", "pos"))` |
| Plot labels and colors | `scale_x_discrete(labels = c("PG" = "Point guard"))` |
| Building a tibble by hand | `tibble(x = c(1, 2, 3))` |

- !! Mixing types forces everything to one type: `c(1, "two", 3)` turns every value into text (`"1"`, `"two"`, `"3"`)
- `1:5` is a shortcut for `c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5)`

## Matching Several Values: `%in%`

`x %in% y` asks, for each value of `x`: **is it one of the values in `y`?** It returns `TRUE`/`FALSE`, so it works inside `filter()`.

```{r}
# Long way: one == per value, joined with | (or)
flights |>
  filter(dest == "SEA" | dest == "PDX" | dest == "SFO") |>
  count(dest)

# Short way: same result
west_coast <- c("SEA", "PDX", "SFO")

flights |>
  filter(dest %in% west_coast) |>
  count(dest)
```

```{r}
# NOT in: put ! in front of the whole test
flights |>
  filter(!(carrier %in% c("UA", "B6", "EV"))) |>
  count(carrier, sort = TRUE) |>
  head(3)
```

- !! `dest == c("SEA", "PDX")` is **not** the same as `%in%`. `==` compares row 1 to `"SEA"`, row 2 to `"PDX"`, row 3 to `"SEA"` again, and so on, so it silently drops matching rows. Use `%in%` for "any of these."
- Also works in `mutate()`: `mutate(west = dest %in% west_coast)` makes a `TRUE`/`FALSE` column
- Order matters: `"SEA" %in% flights$dest` asks one question ("does SEA appear anywhere?") and gives one answer

## Storing Values in Variables

I save new datasets with `<-` all the time, but single **values** can be saved too. It's worth doing when a number:

| Reason | Example from my notes |
|:----------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Gets used more than once | `mystery_seeds <- 10`, then `abs(num_seeds - mystery_seeds)` ([Classification](classification.qmd)) |
| Might change later | `k <- ceiling(sqrt(nrow(fruit)))`: add fruits and k updates on its own |
| Comes from the data, not from me | `obs_diff` from `calculate()` instead of typing `6` ([Hypothesis Testing](hypothesis-testing.qmd)) |
| Needs a name to make sense | `west_coast <- c("SEA", "PDX", "SFO")` reads better than the raw vector |
| Gets quoted in the text | `` `r knitr::inline_expr("round(p_val, 2)")` `` in a sentence prints the current value, so the text can't go out of date |

```{r}
min_delay <- 60 # change the cutoff in one place

flights |>
  filter(arr_delay >= min_delay) |>
  summarize(n_late = n(), pct_of_all = n() / nrow(flights) * 100)
```

- !! Typing a result by hand (`78.46 - 72.46`) breaks as soon as the data change. Compute it and save it instead.
- Names: lowercase with `_` (snake_case), and not the same as a column name. A variable called `dest` gets confusing inside `filter()`.
